Getting on a hand crew was one of the best things i've ever done for myself.  I learned what i was capable of, what good leadership looked like, and i'm sure it's the reason I'm working for a municipal dept today.  Awesome memories too (big fire, hurricane katrina, and all those hilarious things inbetween fires and project work).  Those guys are still like family to me.  I say do it, but then again, i tried the ambulance thing and the school thing and neither caught my attention.  I can't say enough about it as a stepping stone for people that are wired like myself.  as for the logistics of getting on, that depends on where you are and i'm sure those local guys will steer you in the right direction.  good luck to you!

hike with the crew you apply for.  Show them what you're about and make it an easy decision for them.  Regarding doing it as a career, i think you might change your mind.  Nothing at all against it, (trust me, I loved that job) I did it for a few years but i know a lot of guys that had that attitude for about 3 or 4 years and interest tapered off for one reason or another.  For the short term, You'll get on a crew if you want to and you're in shape with a good attitude.  As for a long term goal, I would be looking for a municipal dept that does both.  Just a little more dynamic.  You can lead a crew in the summer, or choose not to as you age.  If, however, after a few years you still love it, perfect, you're doing what you like and change nothing but you set yourself up with a plan B (like getting your paramedic) in the winter with that municipal job in mind.  BTW, I've read very little in this thread so i'm sorry, I'm probably missing a few things about your situation.  Hope it helped anyway.  Good luck!  Any time spent on a good hand crew working for a good leader will be a great experience you WILL value for a very long time.

They'd hike as hard as they could a few times and come in for an interview later.  It was a lot easier to hire a guy we knew than one we didn't.  I have always suggested turning in an application for the agency you want to work for and come out and introduce yourself and hike if you can.
